exercises.name: Ramp-up sets for first main lift

notes: Week 1 is a calibration week. Use RPE 6-7 to establish working weights and assess technique.
Progression (weeks 1-4): Add 2.5-5% load on main lifts when all sets are hit at target RIR. Add reps to accessories first, then load.
Progression (weeks 5-8): Aim to add 2.5 kg to upper-body lifts and 5 kg to lower-body lifts per week where RPE allows. If a lift stalls for two weeks, hold load and add a set or rep.
Progression (weeks 9-11): Top sets climb across the three weeks. Week 11 is the peak; expect the heaviest loads of the programme.
Monday-Tuesday (week 12): Reduce volume by about 40-50% (halve the sets) and keep loads at about 80-85% of week 10. Focus on crisp technique.

Thursday-Friday (week 12): Optional testing. Work up to a heavy single or triple at RPE 9 on squat, bench, deadlift, and overhead press. Stop at technical failure and avoid grinding reps. If fatigued, test a 3-5RM instead.
Avoid hard conditioning on the day before lower sessions.
Warm-up: 5 min easy cardio, then mobility for the day's focus joints, then ramp-up sets for the first main lift.
If sleep, mood, or motivation drop for several days, trim a set from accessories or drop RPE by one point for a session.
Deload trigger: If performance falls for two consecutive sessions on the same lift despite good sleep and food, bring the deload forward.
Log load, reps, and RPE on every main lift.
Check technique on squat, deadlift, and press each week; no load progression until form holds.
Check in weekly on sleep, energy, soreness, and appetite.
Reassess nutrition at weeks 4 and 8 based on weight trend and measurements.
Review the full block at week 12 and plan the next phase.

raw_text:
# 12-Week Strength + Hypertrophy Programme

**Client:** 26F, recreational lifter, combined OCP, cleared for full intensity
**Start date:** Monday 1 June 2026 | **End:** Sunday 23 August 2026
**Goals:** Strength and body composition (build muscle, reduce fat)

## Programme Overview

**Structure:** 4 days per week, upper/lower split
- Monday: Lower A (squat focus)
- Tuesday: Upper A (horizontal push/pull focus)
- Thursday: Lower B (hinge focus)
- Friday: Upper B (vertical push/pull focus)
- Wed/Sat/Sun: rest, walking, optional low-intensity cardio

**Phases:**
- Weeks 1-4: Accumulation (volume, technique, build work capacity)
- Weeks 5-8: Intensification (heavier loads, moderate volume)
- Weeks 9-11: Peak strength/hypertrophy blend (highest intensity, maintained volume)
- Week 12: Deload and testing

**Intensity guide:** Use RPE (rate of perceived exertion) and RIR (reps in reserve). RPE 7 = 3 RIR, RPE 8 = 2 RIR, RPE 9 = 1 RIR.

**Note on the OCP:** No cycle-based adjustments are needed. Programme by training response, sleep, and stress, not by cycle phase. If she reports unusual fatigue, mood changes, or other symptoms, adjust on the day as you would for any client.

## Phase 1: Accumulation (Weeks 1-4)

**Week 1 is a calibration week.** Use RPE 6-7 to establish working weights and assess technique. Weeks 2-4 progress from there.

### Lower A (Monday)
- Back squat: 4 x 8 (RPE 7, week 1; RPE 8 by week 3)
- Romanian deadlift: 3 x 10
- Walking lunge or split squat: 3 x 10 per leg
- Leg curl: 3 x 12
- Standing calf raise: 3 x 15
- Plank: 3 x 30-45 sec

### Upper A (Tuesday)
- Barbell bench press: 4 x 8
- Chest-supported row: 4 x 10
- Incline dumbbell press: 3 x 10
- Cable row (neutral grip): 3 x 12
- Lateral raise: 3 x 15
- Triceps pushdown: 3 x 12
- Face pull: 3 x 15

### Lower B (Thursday)
- Conventional or trap bar deadline: 4 x 6 (RPE 7 to 8)
- Front squat or leg press: 3 x 10
- Hip thrust: 4 x 10
- Bulgarian split squat: 3 x 8 per leg
- Seated calf raise: 3 x 15
- Hanging knee raise: 3 x 10-12

### Upper B (Friday)
- Overhead press: 4 x 8
- Lat pulldown or assisted pull-up: 4 x 8-10
- Dumbbell bench press: 3 x 10
- Single-arm dumbbell row: 3 x 10 per side
- Rear delt fly: 3 x 15
- Biceps curl: 3 x 12
- Overhead triceps extension: 3 x 12

**Progression (weeks 1-4):** Add 2.5-5% load on main lifts when all sets are hit at target RIR. Add reps to accessories first, then load.

## Phase 2: Intensification (Weeks 5-8)

Main lifts shift to lower reps and heavier loads; accessories stay in the hypertrophy range.

### Lower A
- Back squat: 5 x 5 (RPE 8, rising to 8.5-9 by week 8)
- Romanian deadlift: 3 x 8
- Walking lunge: 3 x 8 per leg
- Leg curl: 3 x 10-12
- Calf raise: 4 x 12
- Ab wheel or cable crunch: 3 x 10-12

### Upper A
- Bench press: 5 x 5
- Weighted or assisted pull-up: 4 x 6-8
- Incline dumbbell press: 3 x 8-10
- Barbell or chest-supported row: 4 x 8
- Lateral raise: 4 x 12-15
- Close-grip bench or dip: 3 x 8-10
- Face pull: 3 x 15

### Lower B
- Deadlift: 4 x 4 (RPE 8 to 9)
- Front squat or leg press: 3 x 8
- Hip thrust: 4 x 8
- Reverse lunge: 3 x 8 per leg
- Back extension: 3 x 12
- Seated calf raise: 3 x 12-15
- Hanging leg raise: 3 x 10

### Upper B
- Overhead press: 5 x 5
- Pull-up or lat pulldown: 4 x 8
- Dumbbell bench press: 3 x 8-10
- Cable row: 3 x 10
- Rear delt fly: 3 x 15
- Incline dumbbell curl: 3 x 10-12
- Cable triceps extension: 3 x 10-12

**Progression (weeks 5-8):** Aim to add 2.5 kg to upper-body lifts and 5 kg to lower-body lifts per week where RPE allows. If a lift stalls for two weeks, hold load and add a set or rep.

## Phase 3: Peak Blend (Weeks 9-11)

Heaviest main-lift work, with a top set plus back-off structure.

### Lower A
- Back squat: work to a top set of 3 @ RPE 9, then 3 x 5 at 90% of the top set
- Romanian deadlift: 3 x 6-8
- Split squat: 3 x 8 per leg
- Leg curl: 3 x 10
- Calf raise: 4 x 10-12
- Plank variation: 3 x 45-60 sec

### Upper A
- Bench press: top set of 3 @ RPE 9, then 3 x 5 at 90%
- Weighted pull-up or pulldown: 4 x 6
- Incline dumbbell press: 3 x 8
- Chest-supported row: 4 x 8
- Lateral raise: 4 x 15
- Dip or close-grip bench: 3 x 8
- Face pull: 3 x 15

### Lower B
- Deadlift: top set of 3 @ RPE 9, then 2 x 4 at 90%
- Leg press or front squat: 3 x 8
- Hip thrust: 4 x 6-8
- Bulgarian split squat: 3 x 8 per leg
- Seated calf raise: 3 x 12
- Hanging leg raise: 3 x 10-12

### Upper B
- Overhead press: top set of 3 @ RPE 9, then 3 x 5 at 90%
- Pull-up: 4 x 6-8
- Dumbbell bench press: 3 x 8
- Single-arm row: 3 x 8-10 per side
- Rear delt fly: 3 x 15
- Curl variation: 3 x 10
- Triceps variation: 3 x 10

**Progression (weeks 9-11):** Top sets climb across the three weeks. Week 11 is the peak; expect the heaviest loads of the programme.

## Phase 4: Deload and Testing (Week 12)

**Monday-Tuesday:** Reduce volume by about 40-50% (halve the sets) and keep loads at about 80-85% of week 10. Focus on crisp technique.

**Thursday-Friday:** Optional testing. Work up to a heavy single or triple at RPE 9 on squat, bench, deadlift, and overhead press. Stop at technical failure and avoid grinding reps. If she is fatigued, test a 3-5RM instead, which is safer and still gives a usable estimate.

Record all results for comparison against week 1 and to set the next block.

## Conditioning and Daily Activity

- **Steps:** 8,000-10,000 daily, as a baseline for body composition.
- **Optional cardio:** 1-2 sessions weekly of 20-30 min Zone 2 (easy, conversational) on Wednesday or Saturday.
- Avoid hard conditioning on the day before lower sessions.

## Nutrition

Adjust to her starting weight and preferences; these are starting points.

- **Calories:** Begin at maintenance for weeks 1-2 to measure true intake and weight trend. For body-composition change, move to a modest deficit (about 10-15% below maintenance) or run at maintenance for recomposition, depending on her body fat and priorities. A recreational lifter with a moderate training age can often recomp.
- **Protein:** 1.6-2.2 g per kg bodyweight daily, spread over 3-5 meals (about 25-40 g each).
- **Fats:** About 0.8-1 g per kg, never so low that hormonal health suffers.
- **Carbohydrates:** Fill remaining calories, with most around training.
- **Creatine monohydrate:** 3-5 g daily is well supported for strength and lean mass.
- **Hydration:** Roughly 2-3 L daily, more in hot weather (this block runs through summer).
- **Tracking:** Weigh 3-4 mornings a week and use the weekly average. Take photos and waist/hip/thigh measurements every 2-4 weeks, since scale weight alone can mislead during recomposition.

## Recovery

- **Sleep:** 7-9 hours; this is the largest lever for both performance and body composition.
- **Warm-up:** 5 min easy cardio, then mobility for the day's focus joints, then ramp-up sets for the first main lift.
- **Stress and fatigue:** If sleep, mood, or motivation drop for several days, trim a set from accessories or drop RPE by one point for a session.
- **Deload trigger:** If performance falls for two consecutive sessions on the same lift despite good sleep and food, bring the deload forward.

## Monitoring Checklist for the Trainer

- Log load, reps, and RPE on every main lift.
- Check technique on squat, deadlift, and press each week; no load progression until form holds.
- Check in weekly on sleep, energy, soreness, and appetite.
- Reassess nutrition at weeks 4 and 8 based on weight trend and measurements.
- Review the full block at week 12 and plan the next phase (for example, a hypertrophy-focused block or a strength-specific block).
